entities.summary:
Pope Benedict II was the bishop of Rome from 26 June 684 to his death on 8 May 685, marking the end of a tumultuous period in the Western Roman Empire's decline. During his papacy, Benedict II faced challenges from the Lombards, who had taken control of much of Italy, and struggled to maintain papal authority. Despite these difficulties, he managed to secure the rights of the Church in the region and played a crucial role in shaping the future of the Catholic Church.

As the last Pope of the Old Order, Benedict II's legacy was marked by his efforts to maintain the traditional authority of the papacy, even in the face of growing pressure from secular powers. His death in 685 marked the beginning of a new era for the Church, as the Carolingian Empire rose to prominence and the papacy would be shaped by the influence of Charlemagne.

Benedict II's papacy was also notable for the controversy surrounding his election, which was marked by allegations of nepotism and corruption. Despite these challenges, he managed to secure the support of the Emperor and the nobles, and his reign was marked by a series of important ecclesiastical reforms.

The legacy of Pope Benedict II continues to be felt in the modern era, as the Catholic Church remains a major player in global affairs. His efforts to maintain the traditional authority of the papacy and promote ecumenical understanding have had a lasting impact on the Church's role in the world.

The Pontifical States, which were established during Benedict II's papacy, remain an important symbol of the Church's sovereignty and independence. The legacy of this papacy also serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the integrity and authority of the papacy, even in the face of growing pressure from secular powers.
